about: Regression cases for r2_collect.same_mechanism (kb/Work PB3259): each pair is two findings, or a finding and the filed note of another batch, with the verdict a reader gave them. The pairs of batches 1a and 1b (pin 9e65164eb) are the real records of E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/r2-9e65164eb/batch-1[ab]/collected.json and the landed notes PB2722, PB2725, PB3238; the last two are shaped from PB3259's own measurement.

cases.name: batch 1a: item identification (bound-tree-1 dup #3) is not the ON / NOT ON phrase pair of PB3238

a.rule: One mechanism per job and no semantics in a renderer (DESIGN-architecture-review section 5.1); section 8.1 point (1): lowering-shaped computations are bound-tree and model types, and the bound tree is the model every backend reads
a.target: One identification mechanism in the bound tree: the binder (or the bound-tree computation section 8.1 names) records each statement s identification points as bound structure, the CorrespondingHoist and PairIdentification shape generalized (identified places anchored on MethodLocal positions, re-identification as bound steps), and the backends only render them; PlaceIdentification keeps rendering, and the emitter-side Freeze/IdentifyInto/IdentifyAgain decisions and StringEmitter s Retargeted rebuild are deleted.

b.rule: one rule in one place; two mechanisms for one job (DESIGN-architecture-review section 5.2; dimensions.md 4). The rule each copy implements is the same: the exception imperative runs when the statement's condition holds, the NOT imperative when it does not AND no handled nonfatal condition interrupted the statement (§2023:14.6.13.1.4 GR2/GR3; kb/Work PB1120, PB606)
b.target: one PhraseEmitter.EmitPair(string exceptionCond, IReadOnlyList<BoundStatement>? on, string successCond, IReadOnlyList<BoundStatement>? notOn, string? notGate) (the else-vs-else-if choice derived from whether successCond is the complement) that StringEmitter, ArithmeticEmitter, SequentialIoEmitter.EmitInvalid/EmitNotPhrase, KeyedIoEmitter.EmitDeleteFile and CallEmitter all call, with the hook's NotPhraseGate a required argument for every I-O caller, so a verb cannot render a NOT phrase without saying what gates it; a drift test forbids `Statements.EmitStatementList(not` outside it. Belongs with the DESIGN-architecture-review section 8.3 SequentialIoEmitter split, whose ReadEmitter/WriteEmitter/OpenCloseEmitter would otherwise each inherit a copy

cases.name: batch 1a: the statement edition gate (bound-tree-3 dup #2) is not the quoted literal class of PB2725

a.rule: D7: VersionConformancePass is THE ONE edition gate (DESIGN-architecture-review section 8.3 item (6), DESIGN-version-conformance-pipeline.md); one rule in one place, no recomputation of what an earlier stage resolved (section 5.2)
a.target: every statement-construct gate in the one parse-arm walk (the ENTER check moves to VersionConformancePass, later ProcedureConstructGate per section 8.3 (6)); the binder reads one verdict of that gate for the not-at-this-edition no-op (one helper beside BindIntroducedAt that BindEnter and NamesGatedMessageTag also use) instead of calling Check or IsAvailable itself; the stale comment at 779-780 corrected in the same change.

b.rule: Two mechanisms for one job / one rule in one place (design section 5.2; dimensions.md 4). §2023:8.3.3.2, §2023:8.3.3.4 and §2023:8.3.3.5 fix a quoted literal class by its prefix, and CobolLiteral.ClassOf (CobolLiteral.cs:98-103, enum LiteralClass) is the front end one answer to it, already read by DataBinder, PictureAnalyzer, FileControlKeyRules, LiteralScreenPass and others.
b.target: One quotedLiteral rule (STRINGLIT | HEXLIT | NATLIT | BOOLLIT) referenced by nonNumericLiteral, concatOperand and allLiteral; every consumer reads its class through CobolLiteral.ClassOf and its value through CobolLiteral.Decode on that one node (a small QuotedLiteral reader beside CobolLiteral in Frontend/Common that returns (LiteralClass, value)), and the five per-token ladders plus the VersionConformancePass token tests are replaced by it.

cases.name: batch 1a: the EVALUATE subject intermediate (procedure-binding-4 #1) is not NOT before ANY of PB2722

a.rule: §2023:14.9.13.4 GR3 (each selection subject is evaluated at the beginning of the EVALUATE statement); the PB396 doctrine written at EvaluateBinder.cs:38-49 and SubjectUsage summary (:1054-1058): a single use skips the intermediate only when the render sits in the FIRST arm condition, which the emitted if/else-if chain always executes
a.target: ReadByFirstPhrase holds only when every object before position index in the first phrase is ANY (a constant-true pair that always reaches the next one); otherwise the subject takes the PRE-op intermediate. Add a test of a two-subject EVALUATE whose second subject faults and whose first pair is false.

b.rule: ISO 14.9.13.2 selection-object: [NOT] brackets only identifier-2, literal-2, arithmetic-expression-2, boolean-expression-2 and range-expression; condition-2, partial-expression-1, TRUE, FALSE and ANY carry no NOT. 4.2.2 obliges an indication for source no format admits.
b.target: Keep the superset parse (the doctrine the file states) and screen once in EvaluateBinder: a NOT on an object whose ObjectKind is Any, TrueOrFalse, Condition or PartialExpression is refused by name citing 14.9.13.2 (one new COBOL#### diagnostic), before BoundNot is built; a conformance negative test per refused kind and a positive one per admitted kind (NOT identifier, NOT literal, NOT range, NOT boolean-expression).

cases.name: batch 1a: the generated walk's helper hierarchies (bound-tree-1 arch #2) are not BoundReferences (dup #1)

a.rule: DESIGN-architecture-review section 8.5: the structural walk (b) is generated from the type structure because a hand switch "is total over CASES, not over a case FIELDS" (kb/Work PB26); BoundVisitorGenerator.cs:157-163 names the same bug one level in (a container yielded and not walked through). One mechanism per job (dimensions.md 1); InitializeAction is a closed hierarchy that section 8.5 does not list.
a.target: One structural answer per helper hierarchy: the generator walks THROUGH a non-root abstract record held by a statement by pattern-matching its derived leaves, as it already does for the container roots (Parts_<root>, BoundVisitorGenerator.cs:186-201), or InitializeAction and ValidateStep carry [BoundNode] as container roots (BoundNodeRootPartition_IsExplicit records the decision); the receivers and nested actions of an action are then one generated or abstract member (Receivers, Nested) that ReceivingPlaces, InitStores and InitAct read, so a new leaf is a compile error or is covered by existing; InitializeAction and ValidateStep join the section 8.5 closed-hierarchy list (step 3) for the union conversion.

b.rule: One mechanism per job and explicit registries over reflection discovery (DESIGN-architecture-review section 5.1); section 8.5: the structural walk of the bound tree is never hand-written and is always the generator one (its WALK is always the generator s)
b.target: One generated structural walk: the generator emits, besides StatementChildren and OwnValueParts, the per-leaf enumeration of operand-model fields (places, positions, access paths, counts) that BoundReferences needs, with one rule for collections, tuples and helper records written once in the generator; BoundReferences keeps only its reference policy (implicit operands, nested-statement rule, what a place yields) over that enumeration, and its reflection (FieldsOf, Enters) is deleted. A drift test pins that the walk reaches every non-primitive field of every leaf.

cases.name: batch 1b: a validation entry writing a resolution fact (oo arch f2 #1) is not the OoClassTable god class (f2 #2)

a.rule: Phase boundaries and single responsibility (dimensions.md 1; DESIGN-architecture-review section 5.1, section 8.1): a validation reports, it does not produce model state. OoConformance states this contract itself (OoConformance.cs:98-99, P9 R3: a validation pass reports its findings; it does not mutate the symbol table), and the section 8.3 row for OoConformance plans pure Conforms(left, right) -> ConformanceResult families, where this side effect has no place.
a.target: The §2023:11.6.3 SR5 presented-prototype choice becomes a resolution step of the class table beside ResolveOverrides (OoClassTable.cs:1032): one resolver (OoClassTable.ResolveInheritedPrototypes or an InterfaceSurface type) that runs once the prototype formals are bound, is the one writer of _conformingChoice / Present, and asks the pure MethodConformanceMismatches for the choice. ValidateInterfaceInheritance becomes a pure reporter of the interfaces for which no prototype conforms to all. The order becomes a declared dependency (the INVOKE binding, the IMPLEMENTS check and StorageFormPass require the resolved fact), and the section 8.3 OoConformance row states that its rule families are side-effect free.

b.rule: Single responsibility per type (DESIGN-architecture-review section 5.1; dimensions.md 1); a type over ~800 lines is a god-class candidate (section 3 R0), and section 8.3 designs the decomposition of each one. The census of this pin flags it (R0-0050: 1149 lines, 59 members, 18 fields, fan-in 23, fan-out 55), and section 8.3 (lines 1077-1800 of the design) names OoClassTable only as the host of RepositoryScopeFor, with no decomposition row and no step note.
b.target: A section 8.3 row for OoClassTable: OoClassTable keeps the group lists (Classes, Interfaces, the parameterized, imported and skeleton lists, StandardBase, Names); OoClassTableBuilder owns Build and its screens; OverrideResolver owns ResolveOverrides, MarkRoster, ScreenInheritedPropertyNames and NameMethodSlots (the home of the §2023:11.6.3 SR5 presented-prototype choice of finding oo--architecture--f2#1 too); the per-source-element scopes, censuses and the EntryStore move to the symbol table group tier (SymbolTable.SourceElementScopes in Binding/SymbolTable/, beside ClassNames and RepositoryScope), so a program reaches them without the OO table; RepositorySpecifierAnswers owns the SR6 / SR9 / SR16 questions; ObjectReferenceFacts owns the operand derivations OoConformance and ActivationDescriptions read. Seam: each extracted type is constructed over the built table; no member forwards (rule 4 of CLAUDE.md).

cases.name: batch 1b: OverlappingMove's own over-punch tables, found by two dimensions, are ONE mechanism

sites: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Values/Numeric/OverlappingMove.cs:245-316 (OverlappingMove.SignOf, PutSign, UnpunchAscii, UnpunchIbm, PunchIbm, IbmPositive, IbmNegative)
a.rule: One rule in one place, one mechanism per job (dimensions.md 1; engineering-standards), and ZonedSign own stated contract: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Values/Numeric/ZonedSign.cs:43-53 - THE ONE PLACE EITHER OVER-PUNCH TABLE IS WRITTEN; adding a third convention is a ROW plus an enum member (kb/Work PB803)
a.target: OverlappingMove reads every punch character through ZonedSign (Table(encoding), Punch, TryUnpunch); its libcob-specific dispositions (a plain digit read as unsigned, a foreign byte read by its low nibble, the punched-zero fallback) stay in OverlappingMove as rules over ZonedSign tables, with no character literal of either table and no == SignEncoding.Ibm branch; ZonedSignTableDriftTests gains the source assertion that no runtime file outside ZonedSign.cs spells a punch table.

sites: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Values/Numeric/OverlappingMove.cs:245-316 (OverlappingMove.SignOf, PutSign, UnpunchAscii, IbmPositive, IbmNegative, UnpunchIbm, PunchIbm)
b.rule: one rule in one place (DESIGN-architecture-review section 5.2; dimensions.md 4, one rule written in two places); ZonedSign own contract (src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Values/Numeric/ZonedSign.cs:43-53, kb/Work PB803): encode, decode and valid-sign set are all derived from ZonedSign.Table, and adding a third convention is a ROW plus an enum member, nothing else names a convention
b.target: OverlappingMove reads the punched characters from ZonedSign.Table(f.Encoding) (Positive/Negative IndexOf to unpunch, ZonedSign.Punch to write) and keeps only the libcob-specific dispositions (a non-table byte low-nibble fallback, the adjust unpunch-in-place) as its own logic; no convention is named outside ZonedSign. A drift test asserts no other runtime file spells an over-punch table.

cases.name: batch 1a: the character-position rule re-derived, found by two dimensions, is ONE mechanism

a.rule: One rule in one place (DESIGN-architecture-review section 5; engineering-standards: one mechanism per job); the contract of CharacterPositions (src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Common/CharacterPositions.cs:5-15, kb/Work PB1966, DOC-A.1-157): every site that turns a column into an index of a line, an index into a column, or counts positions asks THIS type
a.target: One definition per assembly boundary, held equal: ReferenceFormatMap.CharacterPositionAt and SyntaxSpanBuilder.Finish call CharacterPositions (same assembly; the compiler through a public CharacterPositions or internals access); the Listing assembly, which by DESIGN-listing.md section 4.2 references no project, gets ONE model-side type (e.g. WiseOwl.Cobol.Listing.ListingColumns: Count, IndexAfter, UnitsAt) that TextListingRenderer and HtmlListingRenderer both call; a drift test in the pattern of DiagnosticRecordsTests.TheSeverityWords_AreTheCompilersWords holds ListingColumns equal to CharacterPositions over vectors with lone surrogates and pairs, and PhysicalLinesDriftTests refuses the surrogate stepping loop anywhere in src/ outside those two types.

b.rule: one rule in one place (DESIGN-architecture-review section 5.2); src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Common/CharacterPositions.cs declares itself THE ONE DEFINITION OF A CHARACTER POSITION (kb/Work PB1966, §2023:6.1 GR1c) and says every site that turns a column into an index or counts positions asks it, but PhysicalLinesDriftTests scans only Frontend/Preprocessor, SeparatorRule.cs and Editions
b.target: One character-position helper the listing assembly owns (an internal ListingPositions with Count/IndexAt/UnitsAt matching CharacterPositions) used by every renderer site; since the Listing csproj references no project, either CharacterPositions moves to a layer both may reference under section 8.1 edges, or the listing copy is pinned to it by extending PhysicalLinesDriftTests to scan src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Listing and src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Listing, with SyntaxSpanBuilder.Position calling CharacterPositions.PositionAt
